rows.reference: LVGL class inventory; rlvgl actor catalog
rows.required_behavior: A director can enumerate every scriptable actor type available on the connected target without prior knowledge of the catalog (MPY-00 §6.2).
rows.baseline_note: No actor catalog exists. `api/src/lib.rs` exposes a fixed `NodeKind` of `Rect` and `Text` with no discovery surface.

rows.surface: Describe type, capabilities, constructors, properties, actions, events, and child policy
rows.reference: LVGL class/property metadata plus rlvgl extensions
rows.required_behavior: One canonical `TypeDescriptor` per actor type answers identity, ancestry/capabilities, constructor inputs, properties, actions, events, child policy, layout capability, and target availability (MPY-00 §6.2, INV-MPY-3).
rows.baseline_note: No descriptor type exists in any crate. Widget schema knowledge is implicit in each widget's Rust API.

rows.required_behavior: An actor of any catalogued type is constructed from a type id plus descriptor-validated constructor inputs, without a per-type call site in the adapter.
rows.baseline_note: Fixed `Rect`/`Text` `NodeSpec` variants exist, but the runtime calls behind them are placeholders in `micropython/src/lib.rs` and the type set is closed.
rows.differences: Classified partial rather than current because the creation set is fixed and the calls do not own a live stage. `NodeSpec` remains compatibility evidence only (MPY-01 §7).

rows.required_behavior: Every operation revalidates an opaque generation-checked handle, and a handle to a deleted actor is rejected with a structured stale-handle error even after slot reuse (MPY-00 §6.1, INV-MPY-2).
rows.baseline_note: `core/src/object.rs` carries detached state, but there is no handle registry, no generation, and no global lookup.

rows.surface: Parent, children, count, index, reorder, and lifecycle
rows.required_behavior: Tree traversal and mutation are reachable by handle, with sibling order and lifecycle observation preserved across a committed batch.
rows.baseline_note: `ObjectNode` already implements the tree semantics; what is absent is stable lookup by identity rather than by held Rust value.

rows.required_behavior: Properties are enumerable and typed, distinguishing access mode, requested from computed, absence from default, and available from unsupported-on-target (MPY-00 §7.2).
rows.baseline_note: `core/src/property.rs` provides `Queryable::get_property`/`set_property` over four `PropertyValue` variants (Int, Bool, Color, Text) on a directly held widget. There is no enumeration, no descriptor, and `set_property` reports failure as a bare `false`.
rows.differences: `Queryable` is an implementation seed, not the scripting contract (MPY-00 §7.2). Existing callers stay source-compatible where practical.

rows.surface: Discoverable actor actions and typed results
rows.required_behavior: Operations that are transitions or collection commands rather than durable state are discoverable, typed, and invoked through the action catalog rather than binding-specific methods (MPY-00 §7.2).
rows.baseline_note: No action concept exists. Equivalent operations are inherent Rust methods on each widget, e.g. `List::add_item` / `List::set_items` in `widgets/src/list.rs`.

rows.required_behavior: Object flags, states, and local style are readable and — where the director owns them — writable, with read-only runtime-authored state clearly separated.
rows.baseline_note: `ObjectFlags` and `ObjectStates` exist in `core/src/object.rs` with native semantics, but no generic descriptors and no declared writability split.
rows.differences: `DISABLED` appears in both `ObjectFlags` and `ObjectStates`; MPY-04 must declare which is director-writable (see MPY-04 PCDN-MPY-04-001).

rows.required_behavior: The director writes requested layout intent — flex/grid configuration, dimensions, constraints, placement, alignment, growth, span — as protocol values (MPY-00 §8.1, INV-MPY-4).
rows.baseline_note: `core/src/layout.rs` implements the layout semantics with native Rust setters; there is no value-typed scripting path to them.

rows.required_behavior: Computed geometry is observable and separately introspectable from requested layout, and is not writable through the scripting contract (MPY-00 §8.1, INV-MPY-4).
rows.baseline_note: Effective bounds are computed and stored by the layout pass, but are not exposed as a distinct read-only scripting surface.

rows.required_behavior: Every emittable event is discoverable with its payload fields, delivery policy, coalescing policy, and applicable actor types (MPY-00 §3, §8.4).
rows.baseline_note: `ObjectEvent` in `core/src/object.rs` is a rich typed enum, but it carries no descriptor, no coalescing declaration, and no per-actor applicability metadata.

rows.required_behavior: Subscriptions are created and removed by token, and active subscriptions are enumerable for a stage.
rows.baseline_note: Native callbacks are heterogeneous Rust closures held by widgets; there is no token, no removal surface, and no enumeration.

rows.required_behavior: Cues are queued and delivered to the director only at VM-safe points; rlvgl never calls into the VM from an interrupt, rendering path, native event traversal, CM4 task, or allocator-critical section (MPY-00 §8.2, INV-MPY-5).
rows.baseline_note: No cue queue exists. `Subject<T>` observers and widget `FnMut` callbacks are invoked synchronously inside native dispatch.

rows.required_behavior: A snapshot of an unchanged stage is byte-deterministic, contains no raw addresses, and marks any truncation explicitly (MPY-00 §7.3).
rows.baseline_note: No snapshot surface exists at any layer.

rows.required_behavior: Bounded resources report capacity, occupancy, overflow, truncation, and backpressure state, and target capability differences are discoverable (MPY-00 §8.4, INV-MPY-8).
rows.baseline_note: `mp_rlvgl_stats` exists in `micropython/mp_module.c` but is a placeholder returning a status code; it reports no capacity or queue state.
